title: Exploration of the correlation between clinical indicators and prognosis in hospitalized children with pneumonia and construction of a risk prediction model based on machine learning algorithms.
summary: In a single-center retrospective cohort of 582 hospitalized children aged 1 month to 5 years with community-acquired pneumonia, XGBoost predicted a composite adverse outcome: stay longer than seven days, PICU admission, or in-hospital death. On a random 175-child validation split, it had AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.78–0.90), accuracy 81.1%, sensitivity 78.6%, and specificity 82.3%, outperforming the compared random-forest and logistic-regression models. Etiology was unavailable for 41.2% of records; no external or prospective evaluation was reported.
ai_technology: XGBoost, compared with random forest and logistic regression; SHAP was used to rank indicators.
organization: School of Medicine, Shaanxi University of International Trade and Commerce

evidence.tested: Retrospective data from 582 children were split into 407 training and 175 validation records. XGBoost validation AUC was 0.84 (95% CI 0.78–0.90), with 81.1% accuracy, 78.6% sensitivity and 82.3% specificity. Top indicators included admission procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, respiratory rate, age under six months and oxygen saturation.
evidence.unknown: This was a retrospective internal split, not a prospective clinical-impact evaluation. Etiologic data were missing for 240/582 children, and no external validation was reported. This was a single-center retrospective internal split, not a prospective clinical-impact evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost integrated admission clinical and laboratory indicators to classify the study-defined adverse prognosis; SHAP analyzed feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
